goals: Explain user-based and item-based collaborative filtering
why: Recommenders drive a large share of viewing on Netflix and of sales on Amazon. They are among the highest-ROI ML systems in business.
explain: Build a **user × item matrix** of ratings or interactions. Most cells are empty: nobody has seen everything.
**User-based**: find users with similar tastes and recommend what they liked. **Item-based**: "people who liked this item also liked…" (more stable, and Amazon's classic approach).

**Matrix factorisation** learns a short vector of hidden "taste factors" for each user and item (for example "action-ness", "romance-ness"). The predicted rating is their dot product. This won the Netflix Prize.

**Cold start**: new users or items have no history, so blend with content features or popularity. Evaluate with **ranking metrics** (precision@k, NDCG) on a time-based hold-out, and confirm with A/B tests.

example.title: User-based prediction for Asha
steps: Ratings on Desert Chase, Highway Heist, Monsoon Letters: Asha (5, 4, 1), Ravi (5, 5, 1), Kabir (4, 4, 2), Meera (1, 2, 5). Will Asha like "Wedding Season"?
Cosine similarity: Asha–Ravi = 46 / (6.48 × 7.14) ≈ 0.994; Asha–Kabir = 38 / (6.48 × 6) ≈ 0.977. Meera has opposite taste (Pearson −1), so she is left out
Neighbours' ratings of Wedding Season: Ravi 2, Kabir 1
example.result: About 1.5 out of 5: do not recommend "Wedding Season" to Asha. Her neighbours are action fans who disliked it.

mistakes: Evaluating with random splits instead of time-based ones (leaks the future).
Optimising RMSE on ratings when the business cares about the ranking of the top 10.
Ignoring popularity bias and feedback loops.
takeaways: Learn from the behaviour of similar users or items
Plan for cold start; evaluate the ranking
use: Many users and items with interaction history
avoid: Brand-new catalogues with no interactions (content-based first)

practice.code:
import numpy as np
# Desert Chase, Highway Heist, Monsoon Letters (the films Asha has rated)
asha, ravi, kabir = np.array([5, 4, 1]), np.array([5, 5, 1]), np.array([4, 4, 2])
cos = lambda a, b: a @ b / (np.linalg.norm(a) * np.linalg.norm(b))
sims = np.array([cos(asha, ravi), cos(asha, kabir)])
wedding = np.array([2, 1])                           # Ravi's and Kabir's ratings of Wedding Season
print(sims.round(3), round(float(sims @ wedding / sims.sum()), 2))   # [0.994 0.977] 1.5
# Production: matrix factorisation (implicit, LightFM) or two-tower neural models

check.q: "Customers who bought this also bought…" is…

options: New users or items without interaction history

formula.plain: User-based prediction: average the neighbours' ratings of the item, weighting each neighbour by how similar their tastes are to the user's (for example cosine similarity).
